newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $69, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $69, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Wednesday were bid $69.00 per cwt, steady with Tuesday's active trade, but owners were so far passing the bids and were pricing cattle at $70.00, feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle prices Tuesday, mostly at $69.00, were $2.00 higher than the bulk of last week's trade.
Gains were tied to a recent surge in beef prices and outlooks for further beef price gains this week, sources said.
About 50,000 head sold Tuesday in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, including three pens of premium cattle at $70.00 to a small packer in north Texas, sources said.

Although the Texas sale at $70.00 was not indicative of the market, it still fueled optimism among feedlot operators that $70.00 could be paid for remaining slaughter steers and heifers that would grade select and choice, they said.
Kansas sales Tuesday were pegged near 35,000 head and Nebraska sales were estimated near 60,000.

Top prices for cattle in Nebraska were $70.00 on a live basis, which further fueled ideas that $70.00 would be paid more liberally further south in the Texas Panhandle area and Kansas, cattle feeders there said.
Packer demand was stoked by renewed retail beef buying, which sparked price advances the past few days.
Heavyweight choice beef Tuesday was quoted up $2.49 per cwt at $105.33, up $6.08 since prices began the current rally, USDA statistics showed.
